objectives.text: Name the stages of the human life cycle and why needs change across them.
Say what governs recommended weight gain in pregnancy.
State infant feeding recommendations for the first year.
Explain why adolescence has the highest nutrient needs outside pregnancy.
Describe how nutrient needs change in old age.
Name the four essential elements of physical fitness.

terms.gloss: Used to track an infant's development against expected ranges over time.
Breast milk only, recommended for the first four to six months.
The rapid growth of puberty, which raises energy and nutrient needs sharply.
One of the four elements of fitness, with muscle strength, muscle endurance and flexibility.
Energy needs fall with age while many nutrient needs do not, so each calorie must carry more.
A chronic-disease risk you can act on — diet, activity, smoking.

questions.prompt: How much weight a woman should gain in pregnancy is determined mainly by:
options: Her BMI at the start of pregnancy
The number of pregnancies she has had
Her age at the time of conception
questions.why: Starting BMI sets the recommended range, which is why there is no single number that applies to everyone.
distractorNotes: Height feeds into BMI but is not the determinant.
Parity is a factor in care, not in this guideline.
Age matters clinically, but not for this figure.

questions.prompt: For the first four to six months, infants should receive:
questions.why: Exclusive breast milk for four to six months, with complementary foods introduced after that.
distractorNotes: Solids come later.
Cow's milk is not recommended in the first year.
Juice is not recommended for young infants.

questions.prompt: Infant development is tracked against expected ranges using:
questions.why: Charts show the trajectory over time, which says more than any single measurement on its own.
distractorNotes: BMI is not used this way in infancy.
Not the routine tool.
Not how infant intake is assessed.

questions.prompt: Nutrient needs are greater in adolescence than at any other life stage except:
questions.why: Adolescent growth is fast enough that requirements rival any other period, pregnancy aside.
distractorNotes: Needs are high per kilogram, but the total is smaller.
Needs generally fall.
Needs are at their most stable.

questions.prompt: Recommended intakes for children are higher relative to body size because:
options: They are still growing and developing
Children lose more nutrients in waste
questions.why: Growth itself consumes nutrients, on top of everything maintenance requires.
distractorNotes: Absorption is not the explanation.
Activity varies and is not the main reason.
Not the mechanism.

questions.prompt: In old age, the usual pattern is that:
options: Energy needs fall but nutrient needs do not
Both energy and nutrient needs rise
Both energy needs and nutrient needs fall away
Energy needs rise while nutrients fall
questions.why: Fewer calories have to carry the same nutrients, so nutrient density stops being optional and becomes the whole problem.
distractorNotes: Energy needs decline.
Many nutrient needs hold steady or rise.
Backwards on both counts.

questions.prompt: The four essential elements of physical fitness are:
options: Speed, power, agility, balance and overall reaction time under load
Running, swimming, cycling and weight training
Warm-up, main exercise, cool-down and rest
questions.why: Fitness is not one thing. A programme strong in one element and absent in another leaves a real gap.
distractorNotes: Athletic qualities, not the four elements named.
Activities, not elements.
The structure of a session, not of fitness.

questions.prompt: Which risk factors for chronic disease can you actually act on?
options: Age, family history and biological sex
Height and your natural body frame
questions.why: Separating the modifiable from the fixed is what turns a risk profile into a plan.
distractorNotes: All non-modifiable.
Non-modifiable.
Non-modifiable.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter treat nutrition as a life-cycle question?
options: Needs change at every stage of life
Because needs are fixed after twenty
questions.why: Every stage has its own demands, and meeting them is what supports health and wellness at that stage.
distractorNotes: Pregnancy is one stage among several.
They keep changing throughout adulthood.
Childhood matters, but does not decide everything.

questions.prompt: Daily energy requirements for preteens differ according to:
options: Gender, growth rate and activity level
The school year that they are currently in
questions.why: Three variables at once, which is why a single figure for an age group is only ever a starting point.
distractorNotes: Height matters; shoe size does not.
Not a determinant.
Not a determinant at this stage.

checklist: Pick a life stage other than your own and name its two biggest nutritional demands.
Say what changes about needs going into that stage, and what stays the same.
Rate yourself honestly on each of the four elements of fitness.
Name one modifiable risk factor you could act on, and the first step.
selfCheck: Did I keep non-modifiable factors out of my action list?
Did I separate energy needs from nutrient needs?
applicationPrompts.aiPolicy: These are questions for you to answer. This app does not write any part of a submission.
